description: AIIR canonicalization trap vectors. Edge cases that commonly differ across JSON encoders in different languages. Conforming implementations MUST produce identical canonical_json, content_hash, and receipt_id.

vectors.description: Commit has an extra uppercase key 'Zebra_field' — tests ASCII sort order where uppercase (0x5A) < lowercase (0x61)

commit.subject: feat: add widget
commit.Zebra_field: should sort after all lowercase keys

commit.subject: feat: add widget
commit.Zebra_field: should sort after all lowercase keys

vectors.implementation_notes: In ASCII/UTF-8 sorting: 'Z' (0x5A) < 'a' (0x61). So 'Zebra_field' sorts BEFORE 'author'. Some languages default to locale-aware sorting which would produce a different order.

vectors.description: files_changed=0, signal_count=0 — integer zero must encode as '0', not 'false' or 'null'
vectors.implementation_notes: In weakly typed languages: 0, false, null may be confused. JSON requires: 0 → '0', false → 'false', null → 'null'. All produce different bytes and different hashes.

vectors.description: is_ai_authored=false — must encode as 'false', not '0' or 'null' or empty string
vectors.implementation_notes: Some serializers coerce booleans to integers. JSON canonical form requires literal 'false'/'true'.

vectors.description: repository=null — 'null' value is different from absent key; both must be encoded correctly
vectors.implementation_notes: A present key with null value serializes as '"repository":null'. An absent key produces no output. These yield different canonical JSON and different hashes.

vectors.description: Nested keys in commit.author must be sorted recursively — date < email < name
vectors.implementation_notes: Canonical JSON requires ALL objects to have sorted keys, not just the top level. Verify that commit.author has keys in order: date, email, name.

vectors.description: repository='' (empty string) — different from null and from absent key
vectors.implementation_notes: Empty string serializes as '"repository":""'. Null serializes as '"repository":null'. These produce different hashes.

vectors.description: Subject contains literal double quotes and backslash — must be escaped as \" and \\ in canonical JSON
vectors.implementation_notes: JSON spec requires: " → \", \ → \\. Verify the canonical JSON has correct escaping.

vectors.description: Subject contains tab, newline, carriage return — must be escaped as \t, \n, \r in canonical JSON
vectors.implementation_notes: JSON spec requires control chars to be escaped. Tab=\t, LF=\n, CR=\r. Some encoders use \u000a instead of \n — both are valid JSON but produce different bytes. Canonical JSON uses the short escapes.
